channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: AppsFlyer expands Agent Hub and MCP tools to automate marketing workflows
item.description: AppsFlyer has expanded its Agent Hub with MCP tools that let marketers investigate and act on their data through automated workflows.

item.title: Building Detailed Caribbean-Inspired City Environment In Unreal Engine 5
item.description: The developer shares the workflow behind Caribbean Alleyway, a scene inspired by the historic streets of Cartagena, with a focus on crafting rich, detailed materials.

item.title: Godot Showreel 2026
item.description: Godot's 2026 showreel is out, with a record 422 community submissions and gameplay from featured projects including Slay the Spire 2.

item.title: Making a sledding game feel like sledding: one engine, three physics configs
item.description: The author shares how six numbers per mode shape the feel of browser sledding game SledRun, with track width and gravity doing most of the work.

item.title: What tech is used to develop GTA 6?
item.description: From C++ and Rockstar's RAGE engine to memory management and frame-time optimization, a breakdown of the tech stack behind a AAA-scale build.

item.title: Microsoft PIX 2611.19
item.description: Microsoft updated PIX, its DirectX 12 performance profiling and debugging tool, to version 2611.19, continuing support for graphics debugging workflows on 64-bit Windows.

item.title: Godot: Make Your Own Video Games for Free, With No Royalties at All
item.description: A beginner-friendly introduction to Godot, the free open-source engine with no royalties, covering its scene-and-node workflow and one-editor pipeline from design to multi-platform export.

item.title: Slot Game Development: The Production Guide Operators Actually Need
item.description: Explains what operators actually commission when they ask for a slot game, as opposed to platform-focused write-ups about sign-up, KYC and payments.

item.title: Host Unity WebGL Games Online: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: No complex platform or pricey server needed — this beginner guide walks through turning a Unity game into a play-in-the-browser WebGL build.

item.title: Ternary logic explained through a hacking game
item.description: In Vesper Protocol, alien machines think in -1, 0 and +1 instead of binary, and this tutorial uses the game's puzzles to explain how to count and build logic gates with three states.

item.title: More Than Prompts: Context and Harness Engineering
item.description: While building a game in Unity with Claude, the author found the AI often stopped silently — the problem was not the prompt, but context and harness engineering failing to give it a clear signal to continue.

item.title: 3 New Tools: The Steam Queue, A Steam Page Checker, and how to make A Steam Page
item.description: Steam's approval queue now takes about a month — this roundup covers the wait, a store-page checker, and how to build a Steam page before you launch.

item.title: Blender Agent Kit v0.2.2: Giving AI Agents a Production-Ready 3D Asset Pipeline
item.description: This open-source Blender toolkit lets AI agents generate 3D assets from scratch that are ready for a game-engine pipeline, catching real production defects and cutting pipeline setup work in testing.

item.title: Clever Weight-Painting Tool For Better Character Deformations
item.description: This weight-painting tool promises smoother, more natural character deformations, worth a look for rigging artists and technical artists.

item.title: This Spider-Man Simulation Brings Back Memories Of Sticky Wall-Crawler Toys
item.description: Developer Duncan Tune recreates the feel of childhood sticky wall-crawler toys with a physics simulation, and shares a peek into his workflow.

item.title: Report: GTA 6 Generated Nearly $2B in Sales by Launch Day
item.description: GTA 6 reportedly sold around 19 million copies and earned $1.84 billion by launch day, potentially one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time.

item.title: I Built a Complete Arena Shooter in Vanilla JavaScript — No Engine, No Libraries, No Audio Files
item.description: VOIDSTORM is a complete arena shooter built in vanilla JavaScript and Canvas 2D — every sound, from the music to laser shots and the boss roar, is synthesized live with the Web Audio API, with no audio files, no engine, no framework and no build step.

item.title: How to Make a Mobile Game Without Coding, and Make It Feel Good
item.description: Describe your idea to an AI game engine and you can ship a real mobile game without writing code — the hard part was never the code, it's the design.

item.title: NetEase Q3 Games Revenue Hits RMB 22.3 Billion; Management Says Short-Drama Boom Is Affecting Games and AI Is Diversifying Gameplay
item.description: NetEase reported RMB 22.3 billion in Q3 games revenue, with management discussing how the short-drama boom is rippling into games and how AI is making gameplay more varied.

item.title: Recreating Minecraft's XP bar with three SVGs and one @keyframes rule
item.description: Three pixel-art SVGs plus one @keyframes rule recreate Minecraft's shimmering XP bar in plain HTML, with no canvas, JavaScript, or GIF, production code and edge cases included.
